quizName: DMV Practice Test #13 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If your motorcycle has convex mirrors and you are not familiar with them, you should practice using them because:

options.text: Most people are not used to using mirrors.
They make objects look farther away than they really are.
They make objects look closer than they really are.
It can be hard to remember to look at mirrors while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make objects look farther away than they really are.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors give a wider view of the road behind you. However, they make objects appear farther away than they actually are. Get used to your mirrors if your motorcycle has convex mirrors.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, which part of the lane should you ride in?
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle increases crash risk. Riding on the far side might encourage the other driver to re-enter your lane too soon.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what does it mean when the lead rider raises their left arm and points with their index finger?

options.text: The group will exit at the next exit.

questions.explanation: Hand signals are important for group riding communication. When the lead rider raises their left arm and points with their index finger, riders should move into a single-file line.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should not:
questions.explanation: To ride safely on slippery surfaces, reduce your speed, avoid sudden movements, and use both brakes gently when braking.

questions.question: When riding in a group, you should:

options.text: Place inexperienced riders at the back.
Not ride too close to other riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not ride too close to other riders.
questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation when riding in a group. Check your mirrors regularly. The lead and sweep riders should be experienced. Keep enough space between riders.

questions.question: Your riding clothes should protect you from all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Motorcycle clothing should protect you from sunburn, windburn, rain, dehydration, cold, and motorcycle parts. Good clothing also provides protection if you crash.

questions.question: If you carry a load in a sidecar, the motorcycle's stopping distance:

options.text: Will be the same as a two-wheeled motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Adding weight to a motorcycle increases its stopping distance. Start slowing down and stopping earlier when carrying a load or passenger in a sidecar.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Decrease the distance between you and the vehicle ahead.
Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed and increase your following distance at night. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther down the road. Be ready to change your lane position while riding at night.

questions.question: When riding a three-wheeled motorcycle through a curve, it is best to:

options.text: Stay in the center of the lane.
Stay on the outside of the lane.

questions.explanation: Three-wheeled motorcycles and sidecars turn differently than two-wheeled motorcycles. The best path through a curve may not follow the curve exactly. You may need to move from the outside to the inside of the curve before straightening out.

questions.question: How should a rider sit on a motorcycle for best control?

options.text: Using arms to hold the body up.
Keeping knees away from the gas tank.
Keeping feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keeping feet firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Sit so you can use your arms to control the motorcycle, not to hold yourself up. Keep your arms slightly bent. Press your knees against the gas tank and keep your feet firmly on the footrests for balance.

questions.question: When are helmets required?

options.text: For riders under 21 or those who have had their license for less than one year.

questions.correctAnswerText: For riders under 21 or those who have had their license for less than one year.
questions.explanation: In Rhode Island, riders under 21 or those with a license less than one year old must wear a helmet. Helmets are recommended for all riders.

questions.question: Which is NOT a good safety tip?

options.text: Lean in the direction you want to go when turning.
Do not drag your feet on the road.

questions.explanation: Slow down before turning and lean in the direction of the turn. Do not drag your feet or you may lose control. Always watch for other traffic on the road.

questions.question: What does proper riding clothing NOT provide?
questions.explanation: Proper riding clothing protects you from injury in a crash and from weather. It reduces discomfort, not creates it.

questions.question: What should your lane position NOT do?

options.text: Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
Invite other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Invite other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps you see better, avoids blind spots, and gives you an escape route. Your position should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane.

questions.question: When carrying a heavy load, what should you adjust?
questions.explanation: Adjust tire pressure, spring pre-load, air shocks, and dampers to the settings recommended for your load weight.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves in a group?

options.text: At the front of the group.
Near the back of the group.
At the very end of the group.

questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should stay near the front, just behind the leader. This prevents them from falling behind and allows experienced riders to watch them.

questions.question: If stopping takes longer than normal, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Leave more space between you and the vehicle ahead if stopping takes longer. Use at least a three-second gap in slippery conditions, heavy traffic, or poor visibility.

questions.question: What type of sign is rectangular?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular with white background and black text. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Choose to either brake or swerve.
Only use the front brake to stop, do not swerve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.
questions.explanation: Do these actions separately, one after the other. Do not brake while swerving because your motorcycle could tip over.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a stopped school bus with red lights flashing?

options.text: You do not need to slow down.

questions.explanation: You must stop completely when a school bus has its red lights flashing. Keep stopped until the lights turn off. The only exception is if the bus is on the other side of a divided highway.

questions.question: When do you not need extra space between your vehicle and the one ahead?

options.text: When you cannot see past the vehicle in front of you.
When weather and traffic are good.

questions.correctAnswerText: When weather and traffic are good.
questions.explanation: You need extra following distance in bad conditions. Add space when the road is slippery, you cannot see around the vehicle ahead, or traffic is heavy.

questions.question: What color vest or jacket helps you be seen best while riding?
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors to be seen better. Bright orange, yellow, red, or green work best. Avoid dark or drab colors.

questions.question: How should you position yourself in your lane when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Stay in one part of the lane at all times.
Move your position based on road and traffic conditions.
Always ride in the center of the lane so others see you.
Ride in a zigzag pattern to get attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. Change where you ride in the lane based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: How do you brake hardest in a straight line?

options.text: Use the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Use the rear brake first, then the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time without locking the wheels.
Use both brakes at the same time while locking the rear wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time without locking the wheels.
questions.explanation: Use both the front and rear brakes together at the same time without locking either wheel for the shortest stopping distance.
